text:
mira: Heads-up — cluster hit sustained GPU saturation in eu-west for ~15m, queues ballooned. Thinking we should revisit fair-share vs dedicated per-tenant pools. any quick thoughts?

alex: saw the spike on dashboards, good call. What pattern of traffic? spikes from a handful of big tenants or broad?

mira: mostly 3 tenants (acct-A, acct-C, acct-D) doing large batched embeddings + interactive chat fallbacks. acct-A is the worst.

zane: If it's a few heavy tenants we can do rate-limited fair-share weights instead of full dedicated pools. preserves utilization.

sachi: Weighting sounds good but worried about tail latency for small tenants — they complain when a single big tenant kills p99s.

jord: Could we hybrid: lightweight per-route FIFO for latency-sensitive routes, and a weighted fair-share for batch routes?

mira: that's the idea I wanted to test. per-route prioritization for routes tagged "low-latency" and a shared fair-queue for everything else. + admission control that dynamically adjusts weights based on GPU occupancy.

alex: how would admission look? token-bucket per-tenant gated by cluster capacity?
zane: we've prototyped a capacity-aware token system: tokens = max_alloc * (1 - util) * weight. when util > threshold, we expire tokens quickly.
sachi: code snippet from prototype:
```
queue_policy: hybrid
low_latency: per_route_fifo
batch: weighted_fair_share
admission: capacity_token_bucket
capacity_thresholds: {soft:0.65, hard:0.9}
weights: dynamic_by_usage
```

jord: important to distinguish soft vs hard thresholds — soft > start shedding low-priority, hard > return 429 fast for top offenders.
mira: agree. Also want to avoid oscillation: if we tighten weights aggressively, big tenants back off and then suddenly reclaim tokens -> thrash. need smoothing window.
zane: implement EWMA on utilization and on per-tenant token refill. 30s window seemed reasonable in earlier sims.

alex: what's the enforcement signal to tenants? 429s, 503s, or long queued responses? We should prefer 429 with Retry-After for predictability.
sachi: +1 for 429. But also surface in metrics/datadog per-tenant: queued_count, avg_wait, rejected_count. owners need to see when they're impacted.
mira: ops question: do we want per-GPU slice enforcement or cluster-wide? per-GPU is more precise but complex with shared KV caches. cluster-wide simpler for routing.
jord: cluster-wide admission is easier for routing policy but may hide hot-spot GPUs. we can add a hot-spot detector to reroute to less loaded racks.
zane: network constraints matter — eu-west racks have ~2x cross-rack latency compared to us-west, cannot reroute freely. need region-aware weight adjustments.
alex: cost angle: dedicated pools cost more but provides predictable SLOs for top customers. Could offer "isolated lanes" as an add-on for high-value tenants.
sachi: let's draft a policy: 1) default hybrid queueing 2) dynamic weights with EWMA smoothing 3) per-route FIFO flags for latency SLOs 4) explicit isolated pool option behind a commercial toggle
mira: sounds good. I'll open a short RFC but we should run a canary in eu-west next week. Anyone want to pair on the admission-control implementation?
zane: I'll pair for the token-refill logic.
jord: I'll handle the routing/hotspot detector.
alex: I'll wire up metrics and 429 surface.
sachi: I'll draft the customer communication for the isolated lanes add-on.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist generated: run canary in eu-west on 2 small racks -> measure p50/p95/p99 and rejected_count per-tenant. Link: https://console/redwood/canary/1745002345
mira: thanks team. we'll sync in #eng-infra-standup tomorrow to lock timelines. :rocket:
